findings.description: Removing "Label PRs" from `workflow_run` also removes the only recompute for a base-branch change. Label PRs fires on `pull_request_target: edited`, and GitHub fires `edited` for a base-branch change as well as for title and body edits. A retarget can create or clear conflicts, so `pr/conflicts` or `pr/ready` now goes stale after one.
findings.suggestion: types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, edited, ready_for_review, converted_to_draft, closed]

findings.description: Dropping "Label PRs" closes only one way in. A fork author can still send the job down the recompute-all fallback (lines 63-69) through `workflow_run: workflows: ["Claude Code Review"]`. `workflow_run` matches the triggering workflow by `name:`. A `pull_request` run from a fork uses the workflow files from the fork's own head, so a fork PR can add or edit a workflow named `Claude Code Review` with a job that just runs (no owner-only `if`). That run completes with conclusion `success`, not `skipped`. For a fork head, `workflow_run.pull_requests` is empty, so `linked.length` is 0 and every open PR is recomputed on every push to the fork.
findings.body:
**A fork can still trigger the recompute-all path through a run named `Claude Code Review`**

Removing `"Label PRs"` from `workflow_run.workflows` closes that route. The remaining entry has the same problem.

- `workflow_run` matches the triggering workflow by `name:`.
- `claude-code-review.yml` runs on `pull_request` (L16-22), and a fork PR's `pull_request` run uses the workflow files from the fork's head. A fork author can edit that file to drop the owner-only `if`, or add any workflow with `name: Claude Code Review`.
- That run concludes `success`, which passes the only check here (`conclusion != 'skipped'`, L44).
- A fork-head run has an empty `workflow_run.pull_requests`, so it falls through to the recompute-all at L63-69 on every push to the fork.

This is the same harm 58d3e5f set out to close ("fork PRs included … recomputed all open PRs"). A fork run held for first-time-contributor approval may also arrive as `action_required`, which passes the same check (medium confidence: platform behavior).

**Fix:** gate the trigger on the run's head repository. This loses nothing legitimate. Same-repo `pull_request` reviews and `@claude review` runs on main both have the base repo as `head_repository`. Fork-head runs never get the review secret, so they are never a real owner review. Fork PRs are still relabelled by `pull_request_target` and by pushes to main.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/58d3e5f2bbfd7ce1088db8be89d03496866d66a4/.github/workflows/pr-status.yml#L39-L44
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/58d3e5f2bbfd7ce1088db8be89d03496866d66a4/.github/workflows/pr-status.yml#L61-L70
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/58d3e5f2bbfd7ce1088db8be89d03496866d66a4/.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml#L16-L22
findings.suggestion:
# A fork's review event gets a read-only token and cannot label; its PR is still relabelled by
    # pull_request_target and by pushes to main. A skipped workflow_run did no work (Claude Code
    # Review fires on every issue comment, and its jobs skip unless the comment asks for a review).
    # A workflow_run from a fork head is never the owner's review, and a fork's PR can name its own
    # workflow "Claude Code Review": with no linked PR it would recompute every open PR.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name != 'pull_request_review' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository)
      && (github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || (github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'skipped' && github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository))

findings.description: The filter `c.name !== "label"` hard-codes labeler.yml's job id. The check run is named after the job id only because that job has no `name:`. The comment above it (lines 98-102) explains the `context.job` exclusion but not the `"label"` one, and labeler.yml has no pointer back. If someone renames the job or adds a `name:` there, the filter stops matching with no error. A failed or in-progress Label PRs run would then count as `pr/ci-failing` or `pr/ci-pending`, and a labeler failure would block `pr/ready`. The bare literal also sits next to `context.job` with no sign that it belongs to a different workflow. Fix: add a short WHY comment that names `labeler.yml`'s `label` job, or exclude by workflow instead (for example `c.app?.slug` or the check suite's workflow run) so the filter doesn't depend on a job id.

Line 8 still says "The workflow names under `workflow_run` must match the `name:` of those workflows", but `workflow_run.workflows` now holds only "Claude Code Review", so the plural is stale. Something like "The name under `workflow_run` must match that workflow's `name:`" fits.
